title: Triggers and Colliders in Godot
summary: Separate solid contact, overlap sensing, and gameplay decisions.
description: Build a door that blocks and detects
framing: A trigger is a broken collider
intro: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Walking through a trigger does not mean collision is broken. It means the region detects you without being a wall. A door shows why one object often needs both roles.
terms: An event another object can handle.
recap: A solid boundary blocks while a trigger detects overlap.
Masks and monitoring settings determine sensor detection.
Transition events need explicit gameplay state and timing.
A door combines a solid panel with an independent sensor.
prompt: Help me build a Godot four door with a solid panel and a larger approach area. Use the same-shaped body and area experiment to demonstrate blocking versus detection. Keep the sensor active while opening, defer physics changes, and track occupancy so an occupied door refuses closure. Test locked, open, occupied, and exited states. Distinguish monitoring from monitorable.
checks: Check: the actor crosses the area but stops at the solid boundary.
Check: opening disables only the panel; occupancy prevents closure.

body.narration: People often use collider to mean a solid boundary, and trigger to mean an overlap sensor. Both use collision geometry. In Godot, the owning physics body or area determines the role. The same rectangle can stop a character or report its passage.
body.motion: Move matched actors toward equal rectangles; stop one, pass the other, mark an entry event
body.why: A spatial comparison makes the behavioral difference visible before code
body.runner_up: A static table cannot demonstrate blocking versus passage
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.topic: Geometry does not choose the role
body.narration: Collision Shape Two D supplies geometry. Put it under a physics body to participate in that body's collision behavior. Put it under Area Two D to define a sensor region. The three D equivalents follow the same separation.
body.motion: Reveal each owner before its shape child
body.why: The actual door tree shows both ownership arrangements together
body.runner_up: A screenshot of unrelated Inspector settings would obscure ownership
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.narration: Here is an actual scripted Godot experiment. Two identical character shapes receive the same movement requests. The upper rectangle belongs to a static body. The lower one belongs to an area. Predict which character stops, and which produces overlap events.
body.motion: Establish both rows, then focus on each equal-sized rectangle
body.why: The engine output anchors the prediction in a runnable setup
body.runner_up: Conceptual motion is reserved for the preceding mechanism
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.narration: The upper character stopped at the solid boundary. The lower character crossed the area, producing one entry and one exit. The geometry was the same size. This result tests this setup; it is not a guarantee about every speed or shape.
body.motion: Move focus from the stopped character to the passed character and event counters
body.why: Actual captured outcome closes the prediction loop
body.runner_up: A shell count alone would hide spatial behavior
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.narration: The player lives on layer three, whose bit value is four. The door sensor has no membership layer in this example, but its mask includes the player. A sensor can detect a target without the target scanning the sensor in return.
body.motion: Reveal the player layer and the approach mask from the executed source
body.why: Real settings connect the directed query to named layer numbers
body.runner_up: A matrix is useful for larger policies, but this is one directed query
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.narration: Our coin detected the player even though the player did not scan pickups. Removing the area's mask prevented detection. That is a directed area query. Do not turn it into a universal rule that every body pair needs reciprocal masks.
body.motion: Show the two actual mask-test records in sequence and hold the contrast.
body.why: Verbatim recorded output establishes the observation and keeps its evidence limits visible.

body.narration: Monitoring asks whether this area detects overlaps. Monitorable asks whether other monitoring areas can detect this area. Our tests disable each independently. For the monitorable test, we move the target out and back before checking the new overlap.
body.motion: Reveal the monitoring test results, then the separate monitorable target results
body.why: Recorded tests distinguish the observer setting from the target setting
body.runner_up: An untested property list would invite the common reversal
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.topic: Choose the event for the target
body.narration: Body entered and body exited report physics bodies. Area entered and area exited report other areas. Our door listens for bodies because the player is a character body. A weapon area hitting a hurtbox area needs the area signals instead.
body.motion: Reveal the body signal connections and their handlers
body.why: The real door script explains the selected API without inventing a weapon implementation
body.runner_up: A broad signal catalog would distract from the target type
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.topic: Overlap results belong to physics updates
body.narration: Overlap lists are updated during physics processing. Moving an object and immediately reading a cached list can show the previous result. Prefer enter and exit signals for transitions. In an automated experiment, wait for the relevant physics steps before asserting the outcome.
body.motion: Move an actor into the region, retain the old cached count, then advance a tick and update it
body.why: A labeled sequence makes timing and stale reads explicit
body.runner_up: A static property reference cannot show temporal ordering
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.narration: Physics overlap callbacks can run while queries are being flushed. Defer changes such as disabling a shape or monitoring. The coin sets a synchronous claimed flag first, then schedules the physics change and emits its value.
body.motion: Highlight the guard, immediate latch, deferred monitoring, and signal in order.
body.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

body.narration: We invoked the collection path again after the first award. The count remained one. Deferring monitoring alone leaves a window before that change applies. A small immediate latch makes the gameplay promise explicit.
body.motion: Reveal the first successful award and repeated-call check from the actual log.
body.why: Verbatim recorded output establishes the observation and keeps its evidence limits visible.

body.narration: An entry is an event. Occupancy is state. Store each entering actor by instance identifier and erase it on exit. Weak references let this door discard actors that were freed. A dictionary also avoids mistaking one actor's exit for an empty room.
body.motion: Reveal insertion, erasure and stale-reference cleanup
body.why: Executed door logic connects edge events to persistent occupancy
body.runner_up: A single boolean demonstration would hide multiple-actor limitations
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.narration: There is no body stay signal in this interface. For a damage zone, enter and exit can maintain a target set, while a timer applies damage at a chosen interval. Decide whether damage happens immediately on entry and how cooldowns work.
body.motion: Mark one enter, several deliberate timer pulses while occupied, then exit stops pulses
body.why: A constructed timeline distinguishes event frequency from game policy
body.runner_up: A code listing would imply a tested damage system we have not built
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.narration: A falling player above an enemy can suggest a stomp, but comparing origins alone is a heuristic. Feet-aligned pivots help interpretation. A top sensor or contact-normal test, plus side and corner tests, makes the intended rule clearer.
body.motion: Contrast a top approach with a side approach at similar heights; keep the heuristic boundary visible.
body.why: The spatial or temporal transformation is the claim; a physical-object metaphor would obscure its exact geometry.

body.narration: This example uses a separate top sensor for a falling player's stomp. A side sensor requests damage. The defeated latch prevents repeated events, and sensor changes are deferred. Simultaneous corner contacts still need an explicit priority policy.
body.motion: Highlight top and side signal connections, then the defeated guard.
body.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

body.narration: This door has a narrow solid panel inside a larger approach sensor. The sensor can notice the player before the player reaches the panel. Detection requests an interaction; it does not automatically authorize opening. The locked setting remains a separate gameplay rule.
body.motion: Focus on the outer approach region, then the narrow blocking panel
body.why: Actual engine capture shows both regions in one reusable scene
body.runner_up: A conceptual door illustration would lose the tested geometry
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.topic: Open the panel, keep the sensor
body.narration: The open method first checks the lock and the open-state guard. It then disables only the solid shape, using a deferred change. The approach area remains active. Removing the entire door would also remove the sensor and its occupancy information.
body.motion: Reveal guards before the deferred shape mutation
body.why: Executed implementation shows exactly what changes
body.runner_up: A before-and-after picture alone hides the deferred mutation
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.topic: Close only when the region is clear
body.narration: The test verifies that a locked door refuses opening, an open door keeps its sensor, and an occupied door refuses closure. After the actor exits, closing restores the solid shape. Multiple actors arriving during closure still deserve a separate stress test.
body.motion: Reveal lock, open sensor, occupied closure and exit restoration checks
body.why: Actual assertions establish scope and leave concurrency limits visible
body.runner_up: A door animation would not establish the guards
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.

body.narration: An area can also influence local gravity or damping; it still does not act as a solid wall. A rigid body can report contacts too when configured. Choose geometry, physical response, event reporting, and gameplay state as separate decisions.
body.motion: Focus on the real nonblocking pickup region and its detected actor
body.why: The tested pickup grounds the role; API extensions are identified in narration
body.runner_up: A fabricated gravity demonstration would overstate the available evidence
body.source: New authored teaching beat; exact code and evidence sources in excerpt-map and FACTCHECK.
